jobs.title: Toxicologist
jobs.description:
Accountable for leading the non-clinical development process through designing and implementing non-clinical strategies for successful development of the company’s lead molecules across all stages of development. Responsible for non-clinical department activities which comprise toxicology, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (DMPK), bioanalytical assay validation and conduct, and biomarkers. The ability to execute and lead sound science-based non-clinical development strategies to support clinical development is a crucial part of this position. Responsible for establishing and culturing interactions with other key groups such as Discovery, Regulatory, and Clinical Pharmacology. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead and provide guidance to the non-clinical group in all matters related to safety assessment, drug disposition studies and bioanalysis related to compounds in all stages of drug development.
Provide scientific guidance to senior management on key issues related to non-clinical development through informal discussions and formal meetings including Program Leadership Teams, Development Review Group, Science Committees and Board Meetings.
Critically evaluate and interpret results of scientific studies and contribute to appropriate sections of INDs, NDAs, IBs and other regulatory documents.
Design and prepare summaries pertaining to toxicology and nonclinical studies to support investigational new drug and new drug application programs.
Assist in resolving nonclinical safety issues through the establishment of novel protocols to solve experimental questions.
Direct and give design input for internal/external toxicology, drug disposition and pharmacology studies.
Serve as key point person to coordinate early activities for a successful transition of nonclinical research to clinical settings.
Provide nonclinical and toxicological updates through presentations to project teams and management as requested.
Coordinate authoring of other preclinical documents – e.g., non-clinical PK summaries and nonclinical pharmacology summaries used in regulatory submissions.
Manage non-clinical development staff including external vendors.
Prepare budget proposals and manage department expenses accordingly.
Assist in the review of vendor contracts and legal agreements as appropriate.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

Ph.D. or M.S. in biological science with emphasis in toxicology preferred.
Professional membership (e.g, SOT or ACT) is desirable.
Experience in the writing and review of regulatory documents (both IND and NDA/BLA) and prior experience with US and international regulatory agency interactions.
Ability to build productive cross-functional collaborations both internally and externally is essential.
Sustained record of achievement in leading toxicology research programs supporting safety assessment of drug development candidates is required.
Demonstrated strong decision making and complex data analysis and interpretation relating to drug development.
Strong communication, organizational and interpersonal skills to work within a matrix setting.

Salary range- 100-140K

jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems. 

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work®
certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking a Water Resources Planner/Scientist
with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth. 

You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery. 

We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California. 

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.  
Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.  
Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.  
Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.  
Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities. 
Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.  
Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.  
Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.  
Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.  
Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.  
Foundational understanding of California water resources and interest in groundwater sustainability, water supply/reliability, watershed management, or climate resilience.  
Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting technical or environmental data.  
Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical information to a variety of audiences.  
Ability to work collaboratively across technical disciplines, stay organized, and manage multiple assignments and priorities.  
Willingness to learn new technical tools, methods, and regulatory frameworks.  
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products.  
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to conduct fieldwork and travel as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Masters degree, coursework, or professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, groundwater science, or another water-focused technical discipline.  
Experience with or interest in SGMA implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans, annual reports, periodic evaluations, groundwater monitoring, or implementation of groundwater projects and management actions.  
Experience with groundwater or surface water monitoring, inter-connected surface water studies, groundwater dependent ecosystems, hydrologic analysis, water quality, managed aquifer recharge, groundwater-surface water interactions, or watershed assessment.  
Familiarity with California water laws, regulations, and programs, particularly SGMA and water rights.  
Experience with GIS, groundwater or hydrologic datasets, databases, modeling tools, or other technical analytical applications.  
Experience supporting grant applications, funding strategies, or implementation of groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects.  
Professional certification or licensure, such as Professional Geologist (PG) license, Geologist-in-Training (GIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification, or other relevant professional credential, or interest in pursuing professional licensure. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $70,000-$95,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information 

Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking an experienced Project Manager, Groundwater & Water Resources
to help lead our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. We are especially interested in candidates who combine strong groundwater and water resources expertise with demonstrated project management and client leadership. California professional licensure, including California Professional Geologist (PG), Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG), or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) is preferred for candidates whose background is centered in geology or environmental engineering. 

This role will focus primarily on Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) planning and implementation, watershed resilience, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning through implementation. The successful candidate will combine technical expertise with strong project management and client leadership skills, working alongside groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, planners, environmental scientists, and other specialists. 

This position is well suited for a technical professional ready to take greater ownership of projects and client relationships while continuing to deepen their expertise in groundwater sustainability and integrated water resources management.

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  

Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Lead and manage SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans (GSPs) and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, monitoring programs, evaluation of sustainable management criteria, groundwater projects and management actions, and adaptive management strategies. 
Evaluate complex groundwater and water resource conditions using hydrogeologic, hydrologic, water quality, land use, and climate information, including groundwater levels and storage, water budgets, groundwater-surface water interactions, groundwater dependent ecosystems, and basin sustainability issues. 
Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies. 
Evaluate and advance nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, watershed restoration, green infrastructure, and related water infrastructure, working with multidisciplinary technical teams to assess feasibility, benefits, constraints, and implementation considerations. 
Lead development of grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, watershed resilience, recharge, water supply, and other water resource projects, helping clients align technically sound projects with available funding and move priority projects toward implementation. 
Direct and integrate technical work performed by multidisciplinary teams, including groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, GIS professionals, and other specialists; review technical analyses and work products for quality, consistency, and defensibility. 
Lead development and QA/QC of complex, multidisciplinary water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and funding applications. 
Lead development of water supply and demand forecasting models using excel-based decision-support tools, addressing water demand factors, passive and active conservation savings, climate change impacts on water use and supply availability, wastewater and return flow generation, and recycled water/non-potable connections.  
Manage projects and client relationships, including scopes, budgets, schedules, contracts, subcontractors, deliverables, meetings, and multidisciplinary project teams across multiple concurrent assignments. 
Lead planning and facilitation of community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input sessions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Communicate complex technical information clearly through technical reports and memoranda, presentations, workshops, public meetings, and discussions with Groundwater Sustainability Agencies, water districts, municipalities, state agencies, stakeholders, and other clients. 
Support proposals, client development, and other business development efforts while mentoring and developing early- and mid-career water resources professionals. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical field. 
Five or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, hydrogeology, hydrology, water resources, SGMA planning and implementation, watershed management, or related technical consulting. 
Demonstrated technical understanding of groundwater systems and hydrogeologic principles, with the ability to interpret and critically evaluate groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data. 
Experience with SGMA or technically comparable groundwater management work, including GSP implementation, groundwater assessments, monitoring, water budgets, sustainability evaluations, or projects and management actions. 
Experience managing projects, including scopes, schedules, budgets, technical teams, deliverables, and client communications. 
Ability to understand and work effectively with groundwater models, water budgets, and other technical analyses and modeling outputs, even if numerical modeling is not the candidate's primary specialty. 
Strong technical writing, QA/QC, presentation, and communication skills. 
Experience working directly with public agencies, water agencies, or other water resource clients. 
Working knowledge of California groundwater and water resource regulations and programs. 
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and work effectively across technical disciplines. 
Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and willingness to travel and participate in field activities as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) or Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG). 
Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical discipline. 
Significant experience implementing SGMA, including GSPs or Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, sustainable management criteria, water budgets, monitoring networks, or projects and management actions. 
Experience interpreting groundwater model results and working directly with modelers on model development, calibration, scenarios, water budgets, or decision-support analyses. 
Experience evaluating groundwater-surface water interactions, managed aquifer recharge, subsidence, groundwater dependent ecosystems, water quality, or other SGMA sustainability issues. 
Experience developing and implementing monitoring programs, field investigations, or hydrogeologic studies. 
Experience with GIS, groundwater databases, hydrologic or groundwater modeling tools, or other technical analytical platforms. 
Experience developing successful grant applications or funding strategies for groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects. 
Experience developing water supply and demand forecast models to support long-range water resources planning efforts. 
Demonstrated experience leading client meetings, workshops, technical discussions, and public or stakeholder presentations. 
Experience developing scopes and budgets, preparing proposals, supporting business development, and developing long-term client relationships. 
Experience mentoring geologists, hydrologists, scientists, engineers, or other technical professionals. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $100,000-$125,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

jobs.title: Service Center Supervisor- Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Bend, OR
jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West is seeking a Service Center Supervisor to join our team in Bend OR!

Responsibilities

Oversee all activities and employees of the location
Project management of all received samples and projects as needed
Analyze microbiology and inorganic testing on potable and non-potable water samples
Perform monthly environmental testing (water, surfaces, air) and annual calibrations
Receive and log potable water and non-potable water samples from clients
Create microbiological and chemical projects and reports and corresponding invoices
Prepare various media types for sample analysis
Submit all compliance drinking water to Oregon State Heath Authority and EPA as needed
Answer and respond to all client correspondence via phone and email
Schedule all equipment calibration and maintain diligent records
Schedule all sample collections performed by the location
Consult public on testing and sampling procedures
Consult water systems and utilities on testing and sampling procedures
Maintain laboratory supply inventory
Maintain all SOPs and training documents
Maintain all NELAP certification requirements including but not limited to: proficiency testing, internal audits, logbook audits, on-site audits by accreditation body and audit responses
Act as onsite Quality Control Officer
Maintain and organize clients chemical and sampling schedules along with bottle orders and personalized CoCs.
Ability to analyze samples on weekends, holidays and on call, as needed

Qualifications

Education/Experience

Associate's degree in chemistry, microbiology, biology, environmental science, or a related physical, chemical, or environmental science discipline required. Candidates must have:
A minimum of 16 semester credit hours in chemistry and at least two (2) years of experience performing environmental chemical analyses, and/or
A minimum of 4 semester credit hours in general microbiology and at least one (1) year of experience performing microbiological analyses, including drinking water microbiology testing.

2 years customer experience preferred

Skills/Qualifications

Aseptic technique
Excellent customer service
Reliable, timely and punctual
Multitasking with strong time management
Work within strict time requirements of microbiology tests
Excellent documentation, computer and organization skills
Must be able to communicate effectively with lab personnel and clients
Previous knowledge of environmental testing and compliance regulations is desired
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Additional Information

Position is full-time salaried, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of longer hours and weekends as needed.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 - $70,000 annually.

Candidates within a commutable distance to Bend, OR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description
: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

Critically evaluate and interpret results of scientific studies and contribute to appropriate sections of INDs, NDAs, IBs and other regulatory documents.
Design and prepare summaries pertaining to toxicology and nonclinical studies to support investigational new drug and new drug application programs.
Assist in resolving nonclinical safety issues through the establishment of novel protocols to solve experimental questions.
Direct and give design input for internal/external toxicology, drug disposition and pharmacology studies.
Serve as key point person to coordinate early activities for a successful transition of nonclinical research to clinical settings.
Provide nonclinical and toxicological updates through presentations to project teams and management as requested.
Coordinate authoring of other preclinical documents – e.g., non-clinical PK summaries and nonclinical pharmacology summaries used in regulatory submissions.
Manage non-clinical development staff including external vendors.
Prepare budget proposals and manage department expenses accordingly.
Assist in the review of vendor contracts and legal agreements as appropriate.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

Ph.D. or M.S. in biological science with emphasis in toxicology preferred.
Professional membership (e.g, SOT or ACT) is desirable.
Experience in the writing and review of regulatory documents (both IND and NDA/BLA) and prior experience with US and international regulatory agency interactions.
Ability to build productive cross-functional collaborations both internally and externally is essential.
Sustained record of achievement in leading toxicology research programs supporting safety assessment of drug development candidates is required.
Demonstrated strong decision making and complex data analysis and interpretation relating to drug development.
Strong communication, organizational and interpersonal skills to work within a matrix setting.

Salary range- 100-140K

new_jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
new_jobs.description:
About Us

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems. 

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work®
certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking a Water Resources Planner/Scientist
with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth. 

You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery. 

We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California. 

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.  
Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.  
Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.  
Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.  
Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities. 
Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.  
Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.  
Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.  
Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.  
Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.  
Foundational understanding of California water resources and interest in groundwater sustainability, water supply/reliability, watershed management, or climate resilience.  
Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting technical or environmental data.  
Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical information to a variety of audiences.  
Ability to work collaboratively across technical disciplines, stay organized, and manage multiple assignments and priorities.  
Willingness to learn new technical tools, methods, and regulatory frameworks.  
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products.  
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to conduct fieldwork and travel as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Masters degree, coursework, or professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, groundwater science, or another water-focused technical discipline.  
Experience with or interest in SGMA implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans, annual reports, periodic evaluations, groundwater monitoring, or implementation of groundwater projects and management actions.  
Experience with groundwater or surface water monitoring, inter-connected surface water studies, groundwater dependent ecosystems, hydrologic analysis, water quality, managed aquifer recharge, groundwater-surface water interactions, or watershed assessment.  
Familiarity with California water laws, regulations, and programs, particularly SGMA and water rights.  
Experience with GIS, groundwater or hydrologic datasets, databases, modeling tools, or other technical analytical applications.  
Experience supporting grant applications, funding strategies, or implementation of groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects.  
Professional certification or licensure, such as Professional Geologist (PG) license, Geologist-in-Training (GIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification, or other relevant professional credential, or interest in pursuing professional licensure. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $70,000-$95,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information 

Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

How We Collaborate

What You’ll Do 

Lead and manage SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans (GSPs) and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, monitoring programs, evaluation of sustainable management criteria, groundwater projects and management actions, and adaptive management strategies. 
Evaluate complex groundwater and water resource conditions using hydrogeologic, hydrologic, water quality, land use, and climate information, including groundwater levels and storage, water budgets, groundwater-surface water interactions, groundwater dependent ecosystems, and basin sustainability issues. 
Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies. 
Evaluate and advance nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, watershed restoration, green infrastructure, and related water infrastructure, working with multidisciplinary technical teams to assess feasibility, benefits, constraints, and implementation considerations. 
Lead development of grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, watershed resilience, recharge, water supply, and other water resource projects, helping clients align technically sound projects with available funding and move priority projects toward implementation. 
Direct and integrate technical work performed by multidisciplinary teams, including groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, GIS professionals, and other specialists; review technical analyses and work products for quality, consistency, and defensibility. 
Lead development and QA/QC of complex, multidisciplinary water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and funding applications. 
Lead development of water supply and demand forecasting models using excel-based decision-support tools, addressing water demand factors, passive and active conservation savings, climate change impacts on water use and supply availability, wastewater and return flow generation, and recycled water/non-potable connections.  
Manage projects and client relationships, including scopes, budgets, schedules, contracts, subcontractors, deliverables, meetings, and multidisciplinary project teams across multiple concurrent assignments. 
Lead planning and facilitation of community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input sessions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Communicate complex technical information clearly through technical reports and memoranda, presentations, workshops, public meetings, and discussions with Groundwater Sustainability Agencies, water districts, municipalities, state agencies, stakeholders, and other clients. 
Support proposals, client development, and other business development efforts while mentoring and developing early- and mid-career water resources professionals. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical field. 
Five or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, hydrogeology, hydrology, water resources, SGMA planning and implementation, watershed management, or related technical consulting. 
Demonstrated technical understanding of groundwater systems and hydrogeologic principles, with the ability to interpret and critically evaluate groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data. 
Experience with SGMA or technically comparable groundwater management work, including GSP implementation, groundwater assessments, monitoring, water budgets, sustainability evaluations, or projects and management actions. 
Experience managing projects, including scopes, schedules, budgets, technical teams, deliverables, and client communications. 
Ability to understand and work effectively with groundwater models, water budgets, and other technical analyses and modeling outputs, even if numerical modeling is not the candidate's primary specialty. 
Strong technical writing, QA/QC, presentation, and communication skills. 
Experience working directly with public agencies, water agencies, or other water resource clients. 
Working knowledge of California groundwater and water resource regulations and programs. 
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and work effectively across technical disciplines. 
Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and willingness to travel and participate in field activities as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) or Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG). 
Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical discipline. 
Significant experience implementing SGMA, including GSPs or Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, sustainable management criteria, water budgets, monitoring networks, or projects and management actions. 
Experience interpreting groundwater model results and working directly with modelers on model development, calibration, scenarios, water budgets, or decision-support analyses. 
Experience evaluating groundwater-surface water interactions, managed aquifer recharge, subsidence, groundwater dependent ecosystems, water quality, or other SGMA sustainability issues. 
Experience developing and implementing monitoring programs, field investigations, or hydrogeologic studies. 
Experience with GIS, groundwater databases, hydrologic or groundwater modeling tools, or other technical analytical platforms. 
Experience developing successful grant applications or funding strategies for groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects. 
Experience developing water supply and demand forecast models to support long-range water resources planning efforts. 
Demonstrated experience leading client meetings, workshops, technical discussions, and public or stakeholder presentations. 
Experience developing scopes and budgets, preparing proposals, supporting business development, and developing long-term client relationships. 
Experience mentoring geologists, hydrologists, scientists, engineers, or other technical professionals.

, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

new_jobs.title: Service Center Supervisor- Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Bend, OR
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West is seeking a Service Center Supervisor to join our team in Bend OR!

Responsibilities

Oversee all activities and employees of the location
Project management of all received samples and projects as needed
Analyze microbiology and inorganic testing on potable and non-potable water samples
Perform monthly environmental testing (water, surfaces, air) and annual calibrations
Receive and log potable water and non-potable water samples from clients
Create microbiological and chemical projects and reports and corresponding invoices
Prepare various media types for sample analysis
Submit all compliance drinking water to Oregon State Heath Authority and EPA as needed
Answer and respond to all client correspondence via phone and email
Schedule all equipment calibration and maintain diligent records
Schedule all sample collections performed by the location
Consult public on testing and sampling procedures
Consult water systems and utilities on testing and sampling procedures
Maintain laboratory supply inventory
Maintain all SOPs and training documents
Maintain all NELAP certification requirements including but not limited to: proficiency testing, internal audits, logbook audits, on-site audits by accreditation body and audit responses
Act as onsite Quality Control Officer
Maintain and organize clients chemical and sampling schedules along with bottle orders and personalized CoCs.
Ability to analyze samples on weekends, holidays and on call, as needed

Qualifications

Education/Experience

Associate's degree in chemistry, microbiology, biology, environmental science, or a related physical, chemical, or environmental science discipline required. Candidates must have:
A minimum of 16 semester credit hours in chemistry and at least two (2) years of experience performing environmental chemical analyses, and/or
A minimum of 4 semester credit hours in general microbiology and at least one (1) year of experience performing microbiological analyses, including drinking water microbiology testing.

2 years customer experience preferred

Skills/Qualifications

Aseptic technique
Excellent customer service
Reliable, timely and punctual
Multitasking with strong time management
Work within strict time requirements of microbiology tests
Excellent documentation, computer and organization skills
Must be able to communicate effectively with lab personnel and clients
Previous knowledge of environmental testing and compliance regulations is desired
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Additional Information

Position is full-time salaried, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm with possibility of longer hours and weekends as needed.

The salary range for this position is $65,000 - $70,000 annually.

Candidates within a commutable distance to Bend, OR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
We are well on our way to achieving our objective of carbon neutrality by 2025, through a combination of emission reduction and compensation initiatives. We encourage our laboratory leaders to make sustainable changes at their local level, and in addition to their initiatives we also count on our dedicated carbon reduction team to help us to achieve this goal!

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description
: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.
